hints: Since the ring is smooth, the tension $T$ is uniform throughout sections $AR$ and $BR$ of the string.
Section $AR$ is inclined at $70^\circ$ above the horizontal, and section $BR$ is perpendicular to the $45^\circ$ roof, so it is inclined at $45^\circ$ above the horizontal.
Resolve vertically in equilibrium to find $T$: $T\sin 70^\circ + T\sin 45^\circ = mg$ with $m = 0.2\text{ kg}$ and $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Resolve horizontally in equilibrium to find $P$: $P + T\cos 70^\circ = T\cos 45^\circ$.
walkthrough: Because the ring is smooth, the tension $T$ is the same in both sections $AR$ and $BR$. Section $AR$ is inclined at $70^\circ$ to the horizontal, and section $BR$ is perpendicular to the $45^\circ$ slope, meaning it is inclined at $45^\circ$ to the horizontal.

Resolve forces vertically in equilibrium ($m = 0.2\text{ kg}$, $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$):
$$T\sin 70^\circ + T\sin 45^\circ = mg$$
$$T\left(\sin 70^\circ + \sin 45^\circ\right) = 0.2(10) = 2$$
$$T(0.939693 + 0.707107) = 2$$
$$1.646800T = 2 \implies T = \frac{2}{1.646800} \approx 1.2145\text{ N} \approx 1.21\text{ N}$$

Resolve forces horizontally in equilibrium:
$$P + T\cos 70^\circ = T\cos 45^\circ$$
$$P = T\left(\cos 45^\circ - \cos 70^\circ\right)$$
$$P = 1.21447(0.707107 - 0.342020) = 1.21447(0.365087) \approx 0.4434\text{ N} \approx 0.443\text{ N}$$
teacher_walkthrough: State the mechanical principle for a smooth ring on a light string: the tension $T$ is uniform throughout both segments $RA$ and $RB$.

Determine the angles of the string segments relative to the horizontal:
- Segment $RA$ makes an angle of $70^\circ$ above the horizontal (directed upwards and to the right).
- Segment $RB$ is perpendicular to the $45^\circ$ inclined roof, so its angle with the horizontal is $90^\circ - 45^\circ = 45^\circ$ (directed upwards and to the left).
- The horizontal force $P$ acts to the right, and the weight $W = mg = 0.2 \times 10 = 2\text{ N}$ acts vertically downwards.

Set up the vertical equilibrium equation:
$$\Sigma F_y = 0 \implies T\sin 70^\circ + T\sin 45^\circ - mg = 0$$
$$T(\sin 70^\circ + \sin 45^\circ) = 2$$
Evaluate the sines:
$$\sin 70^\circ \approx 0.939693, \quad \sin 45^\circ \approx 0.707107$$
$$\sin 70^\circ + \sin 45^\circ = 1.646800$$
Solve for $T$:
$$T = \frac{2}{1.646800} \approx 1.21447\text{ N} \approx 1.21\text{ N}$$

Set up the horizontal equilibrium equation (taking rightwards as positive):
$$\Sigma F_x = 0 \implies P + T\cos 70^\circ - T\cos 45^\circ = 0$$
$$P = T(\cos 45^\circ - \cos 70^\circ)$$
Evaluate the cosines:
$$\cos 45^\circ \approx 0.707107, \quad \cos 70^\circ \approx 0.342020$$
$$\cos 45^\circ - \cos 70^\circ = 0.365087$$
Substitute $T = 1.21447\text{ N}$:
$$P = 1.21447 \times 0.365087 \approx 0.44339\text{ N} \approx 0.443\text{ N}$$

ai_rubric.Applying Coplanar Equilibrium: Resolves vertically to find $T = 1.21\text{ N}$ and horizontally to find $P = 0.443\text{ N}$.
ai_rubric.Resolving Forces Along Chosen Axes: Correctly resolves string tensions and forces along horizontal and vertical directions.
